summary: Today’s pulse tracks Southern and central Australia face summer of heightened bushfire risk and heatwaves, Two Italians killed in strike in Kuwait, as Iran denies responsibility, and Coalition team up with Labor to pass 20% gas reservation scheme for Australia’s largest exporters. Across Guardian and BBC, the strongest repeated signals are australia, since, and country. In the background, ‘Disaster’ unfolding as Sydney fire ant outbreak partly blamed on ignored biosecurity recommendations and Israeli strikes kill 16 schoolchildren so far this month, Gaza ministry says keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Southern and central Australia face summer of heightened bushfire risk and heatwaves
headlines.description: Fire chiefs say large swathes of the country are at risk from fires driven by high fuel loads, dry soil and hot weather Most of Victoria, eastern Tasmania and large parts of South Australia, Western Australia, New South Wales and the Northern Territory face heightened bushfire risk – driven by high fuel loads, low soil moisture and forecast hot and dry conditions – according to the seasonal outlook from the Australian and New Zealand Council for Fire and Emergency Services (AFAC), released on Friday.

headlines.title: Two Italians killed in strike in Kuwait, as Iran denies responsibility
headlines.description: The pair were technicians for German company Rheinmetall, according to Italy's foreign ministry.

headlines.title: Coalition team up with Labor to pass 20% gas reservation scheme for Australia’s largest exporters
headlines.description: Coalition voted in Senate to pass government’s final major piece of legislation for 2026, denying Greens’ bid for 25% tax on exports The opposition voted with the government in the Senate on Thursday night in a late sitting, giving Labor the numbers it needed. headlines.title: ‘Disaster’ unfolding as Sydney fire ant outbreak partly blamed on ignored biosecurity recommendations
headlines.description: Farmers’ Federation president says Australia ‘can’t even keep [illicit] cigarettes out of the country … let alone some of these difficult-to-detect pests’ Environmentalists and biosecurity experts warn the large colony of red imported fire ants are a warning sign that the country’s quarantine system is too slow-moving, underfunded and overly concerned with agriculture.

headlines.title: Israeli strikes kill 16 schoolchildren so far this month, Gaza ministry says
headlines.description: Statement follows death of sisters, aged 15 and 13, in airstrike on residential apartment in Gaza City Israeli strikes have killed at least 16 schoolchildren in Gaza since the start of November, as young people across the territory face intensifying bombardment and a struggle to find food, clean water and shelter. On Wednesday, Gaza’s ministry of education said: “Palestinian students had been targeted for the third time in less than 24 hours, in an escalation reflecting the continued Israeli violations against children in the Gaza Strip. The number of schoolchildren killed since the beginning of November has now risen to 16.”

headlines.title: Net migration to UK falls to lowest level since 1997 excluding pandemic
headlines.description: Latest figures show difference between number of people arriving and leaving UK was ⁠77,000 in ​year ‌to ‌June Analysis: How much of the fall in UK immigration is due to Labour’s policies? Net migration across the UK has fallen to its lowest level since 1997 with the exclusion of the years of the Covid pandemic. Figures released by the Office for National Statistics and the Home Office show that the difference between people arriving and leaving the UK was ⁠77,000 in ⁠the ​year ‌to ‌June ‌2026.

headlinePool.title: Nottingham man jailed for 12 years for drugging and sexually assaulting partner
headlinePool.description: ‘Depraved’ predator attacked victim while she was under the influence of sleeping tablets he had given her A man has been jailed for 12 years for drugging his long-term partner and sexually assaulting her while she slept. The man, who is in his 30s and from Nottingham, cannot be named in order to protect the identity of his victim. At a hearing in June, he admitted sexually assaulting the woman on multiple occasions while she was under the influence of sleeping pills.

headlinePool.title: Trump alleges ‘fake’ economic figures released before US midterms but doesn’t provide evidence
headlinePool.description: In a Thanksgiving post, the US president seeks investigation after blue wave of Democrats unseat Republicans Donald Trump has alleged without evidence that economic figures published by the US federal government before this month’s midterm elections were “fake” and demanded an investigation after voters roundly rejected his Republican party. In a holiday message on social media tinged with bitterness, the US president wished a happy thanksgiving “to even those who issued fake Economic Numbers, just prior to the Election, and corrected them yesterday, three weeks late, showing that the GDP was actually 4.3%, versus 3.4%”.

headlinePool.title: How much of the sharp fall in UK immigration is due to Labour’s policies?
headlinePool.description: Labour is jubilant it has got numbers down to levels the Tories could not but it was helped by factors beyond its control Net migration to UK falls to lowest level since 1997 excluding pandemic David Cameron was the leader of the opposition when he made a comment on overall migration that was used to interrogate every Tory leader for the next 14 years. Asked in January 2010 on the BBC by the interviewer Andrew Marr to address comments made by the archbishop of Canterbury calling for the population to remain under 70 million, Cameron said net immigration levels of 200,000 a year were “too much”.

headlinePool.title: Watch: Roofs torn off and streets under water as severe weather hits US
headlinePool.description: Hundreds of thousands have been affected by storms in the country as the Thanksgiving holiday weekend begins.

headlinePool.title: US Senate ‘permitting bill’ threatens clean water protections to speed up energy projects
headlinePool.description: The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act passed the Senate and is now being debated in the House An industry-backed “permitting bill” approved by the US Senate would gut key clean water protections with changes that would do little to speed up the development of major energy projects, advocates warn. The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 (Baaja) passed the Senate 62-33 and is now being debated in the House. The Baaja is a “permitting reform” bill that aims to reduce the time it takes federal agencies to approve major energy and infrastructure projects, like power lines, fossil fuel pipelines, natural gas plants and datacenters .

headlinePool.title: Oxford museum displays seized belongings of Naga freedom fighter Gaidinliu for first time
headlinePool.description: Notebooks, clothes and ritual objects taken by British forces in India in the 1930s go on show at Pitt Rivers Museum In 1932, British forces in north-east India imprisoned a 17-year-old girl called Gaidinliu for leading an uprising against colonial rule. While pursuing the freedom fighter through hills and valleys in the homeland of the Naga people, colonial officers also seized some of her most treasured possessions. They were sent to the University of Oxford’s Pitt Rivers Museum and kept in storage. Now, for the first time, the museum is exhibiting the collection of 27 items, including a basket of Gaidinliu’s notebooks believed to contain her prophetic visions as the leader of a Naga Indigenous religion, clothes, bracelets and amulets.

headlinePool.title: Fifa confirms cyber-attack exposed ‘personal and business information’
headlinePool.description: Football’s governing body says hackers accessed a limited set of personal and business data Fifa confirmed that hackers gained access to a “limited set of personal and business information” in a cyber-attack, amid heightened concern over digital vulnerabilities of leading organizations and institutions. The global soccer governing body said it “condemns in the strongest possible terms the unlawful acquisition and publication of information, particularly personal data”, in a statement to the Associated Press on Thursday. “Such actions constitute a serious and unacceptable violation of privacy and can have significant consequences for the individuals concerned.”

headlinePool.title: Number of Neets in UK falls below a million as Burnham pushes to tackle crisis
headlinePool.description: Latest figure of young people not in education, employment or training remains close to highest level in a decade Business live – latest updates UK politics live – latest updates The number of young people across the UK not in education, employment or training (Neet) has decreased but remains close to a million as Andy Burnham’s government pushes to tackle Britain’s youth jobs crisis. As ministers prepare to make sweeping changes in response to Alan Milburn’s landmark report on young people and work, the Office for National Statistics said the number of Neets fell by 22,000 in the three months to September, to 959,000.

headlinePool.title: Hospitals in England brace for flu spike with admissions highest for time of year since pre-Covid
headlinePool.description: NHS chief says hospital bosses should consider asking staff and visitors to wear masks as winter pressures build Hospitals are bracing for a “horrible spike” in flu in the coming days as winter starts to bite, the head of the NHS in England has said. Flu and other winter viruses including Covid pose such a threat that hospital bosses should consider telling staff and visitors to wear masks, Jim Mackey said, as figures showed rates of admissions to hospital with flu were at the highest for the time of year since before Covid.
